summary: Senegal permits dual citizenship. Senegalese born abroad or Senegalese who have naturalized abroad can retain or reclaim their Senegalese nationality. The country has strong diaspora ties, especially with France and North America.

citizenship.dualCitizenshipNote: Senegal's Code de la Nationalité Sénégalaise (Nationality Code) permits dual citizenship. Senegalese nationals do not automatically lose citizenship by acquiring foreign nationality.

diasporaProgram.name: Senegalese Citizenship / Nationality by Descent
diasporaProgram.statusNote: Active. Senegal has an extensive diaspora, estimated at 3 million people, and maintains strong consular services. Senegalese by descent can apply for nationality through the Ministry of Justice.
diasporaProgram.eligibility: Persons born to a Senegalese father (or mother under specific conditions). Children born abroad to Senegalese parents are Senegalese by birth.
diasporaProgram.applicationFeeNote: Contact the Senegalese Embassy or Ministry of Justice for current fees. Fees are denominated in West African CFA francs.
keyDocuments: Senegalese parent's birth certificate or ID (Carte Nationale d'Identite)
processSteps: Contact nearest Senegalese Embassy or Consulate
Documents processed by Ministry of Justice in Dakar
Senegalese nationality certificate and passport issued
diasporaProgram.verificationNote: Based on Senegalese Nationality Code provisions. Official government website primarily in French. Embassy contact recommended for English-speaking applicants.

keyFacts: Dual citizenship permitted, Senegalese don't lose citizenship by naturalizing abroad
Citizenship by descent available through Senegalese parent
Large diaspora in France, Italy, Spain, USA, and Gabon
Official process in French, embassy assistance available
Dakar is a growing hub for West African diaspora entrepreneurs
whyItMatters: Senegal's pro-diaspora stance is well-established. With a large and influential diaspora sending remittances that constitute a significant share of GDP, Senegal has strong incentive to maintain diaspora citizenship connections. The process works through the embassy system.
